title: Performance-only result (v1)
description: Machine-readable record of a PERFORMANCE-ONLY change: a candidate that computes the same search result faster (or with fewer resources) and makes no tactical, strategic, evaluation, pruning, ordering or move-selection change. Per INV-2, such a change is accepted on measured behavioral identity + a repeatable speedup, and must NOT claim Elo. Any change that alters what the engine decides is NOT performance-only and needs an SPRT record (INV-1, sprt-result.schema.json).

changeClass.description: Self-declared class. Only performance-only changes may use this record.

parity.description: Paired cold fixed-node searches. Non-timing output must be identical, else the change is not performance-only.

minSpeedupPct.description: Worst measured repeat: must stay above -2% (a deeper dip is a real regression, not noise).

repeatsPositive.description: Repeats where the candidate was faster.

repeatsTotal.description: Timed repeats; must equal `repeats`. At least 5 to accept.

signTestP.description: One-sided sign test P(X >= repeatsPositive), X ~ Binomial(repeatsTotal, 0.5). Must be <= 0.05 to accept.

resources.description: Material resource cost of the speedup. A gain bought with memory is not free.

strengthClaim.description: A performance-only record never claims an Elo gain. Strength evidence goes in an SPRT record.

screen.description: Optional equal-clock sanity screen. Informational only: it can neither promote nor block a performance-only change unless it shows a loss beyond noise (that is a bug, not a slowdown).

decision.description: accept_performance REQUIRES: full parity, zero failing tests, medianSpeedupPct >= 2.0, a consistent speedup (sign test p <= 0.05 over >= 5 repeats), no repeat below -2%, resource deltas <= 5%, strengthClaim false.
